security_spec.violation_condition: FreeBSD kernel interrupt handlers or scheduler assume same-level interrupt nesting (old iprio[i] threshold permitting higher-priority interrupts within a level to preempt), but hardware following the new spec sets sithreshold to IPRIO (the level's maximum priority), silently blocking all same-level nesting and starving time-critical handlers.
security_spec.summary: sithreshold on trap entry changed from per-interrupt priority (iprio[i]) to level-max priority (IPRIO), blocking all same-level nested interrupts that FreeBSD may rely on

findings.finding: PLIC threshold is correctly set to 0 (accept all priorities) on all CPUs. No AIA CSR (sithreshold/sipstatus/iprio) is touched, so the Smnip vulnerability pattern does not apply to the current PLIC path.
APLIC threshold is explicitly disabled (set to 0) for all CPUs, matching the accept-all-priorities behavior. No AIA supervisor-level CSRs (sithreshold, sipstatus, iprio) are accessed.

Interrupt dispatch calls intr_irq_handler() with critical_enter() protection. Interrupt nesting is tracked via td_intr_nesting_level, not through any CSR-based priority/threshold mechanism. No iprio/sithreshold interaction exists.

The local interrupt controller (INTC) handler dispatches individual IRQs based on scause. It uses only standard S-mode CSRs (sie, sstatus) for enable/disable. No Smnip/AIA registers (sithreshold, sipstatus, iprio) are referenced.
VMM correctly saves/restores hvip for guest interrupt injection, but does not reference hviprio, sithreshold, or sipstatus. Since Smnip is not implemented in this tree, there is no vulnerability.
findings.snippet:
csr_write(hvip, csrs->hvip);
/* No hviprio, sithreshold, sipstatus handling */

findings.finding: Context switch saves/restores only standard registers (ra, sp, s0-s11, FPE). No AIA CSRs are saved or restored, which is correct because the current code does not use them. No violation.

Boot sequence sets stvec and initializes sscratch to 0. No sithreshold or other AIA CSRs are configured. Since the kernel does not depend on CSR-based interrupt prioritization, this is correct for the current PLIC/APLIC hardware model.
findings.snippet:
la t0, cpu_exception_handler
csrw stvec, t0
/* Ensure sscratch is zero */
li t0, 0
csrw sscratch, t0
